page: Amazon Web Services m8g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 silicon. It features 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Memory is provisioned at 16 GB, adhering to a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM balance. The instance does not include bundled local storage or hardware accelerators, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps for external communication and remote storage access.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent middle-tier performance across integer computation and network input/output tasks. The instance demonstrates steady outputs in stress-ng multi-core testing at 6818.16 and large-block memory read bandwidth at 96.39 GB/sec. Application-oriented tests record 9.39 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.08 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression yields strong execution at 14.17 GB/sec. Conversely, PassMark CPU tests show weaker results in cryptographic and extended instruction evaluations, and small-model language inference speeds remain limited.

By providing dedicated physical execution cores rather than virtual hyperthreads, the server avoids CPU contention issues common in shared core topologies. The platform yields steady cost efficiency for arm64-native applications, though deployments must accommodate the lack of integrated NVMe disks by utilizing network-attached volumes. The instance profile is well suited for web serving, microservices, continuous integration pipelines, and in-memory caching systems.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 16 GB of system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, paired with 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and providing a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps under the AWS Nitro hypervisor. In benchmark tests, the instance shows consistent mid-tier performance across stress-ng compute, Geekbench suites, Redis SET operations at 9.39 million ops/sec, and static web serving throughput at 10.08 GB/sec, though instruction-intensive encryption tests and LLM inference fall into lower performance percentiles. Balancing dedicated hardware resources without hyperthreading overhead, it offers qualitative operational efficiency for general-purpose workloads, including web servers, application runtimes, and distributed microservices.
